A.name: IDENTITY_CATEGORY
A.purpose: Practice be + noun phrase only where natural; controlled transfer is explicitly marked when the source does not naturally supply an identity sentence.

B.name: DESCRIPTION_STATE
B.purpose: Practice be + adjective/state language grounded in the episode.

C.name: LOCATION
C.purpose: Practice be + place/location language grounded in the episode.

D.name: SUBJECT_BE_REFERENCE_SHIFT
D.purpose: Preserve the same fact while shifting a name/noun phrase to a pronoun so subject-be agreement becomes visible without a grammar table.

E.name: AFFIRMATIVE_NEGATIVE_CONTRAST
E.purpose: Contrast affirmative and negative be meanings when source truth or a safe semantic inference supports the contrast.

F.name: CONNECTED_BE_SENTENCES
F.purpose: Combine two compatible be facts into natural connected A1 sentences.

G.name: CONTEXTUAL_TRANSFER
G.purpose: Apply the same sentence family to a nearby context. These examples are pedagogical transfer and are explicitly not source facts.

A.name: IDENTITY_CATEGORY
examples: This is the bathroom.
This is my blue towel.

B.name: DESCRIPTION_STATE
examples: The room is small and bright.
I am clean and ready for the day.

C.name: LOCATION
examples: My blue towel is near the door.
My bag is outside the room.
The mirror is above the sink.

D.name: SUBJECT_BE_REFERENCE_SHIFT
examples: My blue towel is near the door.
It is near the door.
My bag is outside the room.
It is outside the room.

E.name: AFFIRMATIVE_NEGATIVE_CONTRAST
examples: I am in the bathroom.
I am not outside the room.
My bag is outside the room.
My bag is not in the bathroom.

F.name: CONNECTED_BE_SENTENCES
examples: The room is small and bright, and I am clean and ready.
My towel is near the door, and my bag is outside the room.

G.name: CONTEXTUAL_TRANSFER
examples: My coat is near the door.
My shoes are outside the room.
